passage:
After his night rounds, Harish stayed on in the hospital's biomedical workshop and pulled out the service logbook for the ICU machines. Six entries in March, all signed by Suresh, his senior and friend, who had taught him everything in his first week.
He checked the gate register. Suresh had been on leave on four of those dates.
Maybe someone else signed for him. Maybe the dates were copied wrong. Harish wrote it all down, dates side by side, and went to see Ojas in stores.
'Did we issue filters for the ICU machines in March?'
Ojas scrolled. 'Nothing since January.'
Harish walked back slowly. He thought of Suresh's daughter's wedding card on the workshop wall. Then of the patients on those machines tonight.
He needed to be sure. He wasn't yet.

qa.q: On how many of the six March dates was Suresh on leave?
qa.a: Suresh had been on leave on four of those dates.

qa.q: What conflicting feelings does Harish have as he walks back?
qa.a: He feels loyalty and affection for Suresh, who taught him everything, and worry for the patients on the machines tonight.

qa.q: What is wise about how Harish is handling this stage?
qa.a: He is quietly gathering facts, checking other records and considering innocent explanations, so he is sure it is real before raising it.

qa.q: What might the ICU patients' families be trusting in without knowing it?
qa.a: They are trusting that the machines their relatives depend on have really been serviced.

grounding: It shows an employee quietly checking records, considering innocent explanations and weighing loyalty to a colleague against patients' safety.

passage:
Subject: can you tell me if I'm being paranoid
Hi Lavanya,
You know accounts much better than me, so I need a sanity check. No names, just the shape of it.
At work I process vendor payments. One cleaning supplier gets paid every month, but I've never seen their staff in the building, and our floors are cleaned by the in-house team. I looked up the supplier's address on the invoice. It's the same building as my manager's flat.
I've gone through every invoice for a year and listed them. I asked facilities, casually, who the outside cleaners were. They didn't know of any.
Maybe it's a sub-contract I don't understand. My manager has been kind to me. I don't want to ruin someone over a mistake.
Is there an innocent explanation I'm missing?
Charu

qa.q: Whose flat is in the same building as the supplier's address?
qa.a: The supplier's address is the same building as Charu's manager's flat.

qa.q: What is Charu worried about in asking Lavanya?
qa.a: Charu worries about being wrong and ruining a kind manager over a mistake, while also feeling uneasy that the payments may be fake.

qa.q: What makes Charu's approach sensible at this stage?
qa.a: Charu is gathering facts quietly, checking with facilities and asking an informed friend for innocent explanations before deciding whether to act.

qa.q: How might Lavanya feel receiving this email?
qa.a: Lavanya may feel trusted and a little concerned, wanting to help Charu think it through carefully.

grounding: It shows an employee quietly gathering facts about suspicious payments and asking whether there is an innocent explanation before acting.

passage:
Dear Nandini,
I need a sensible friend. Something at the school trust has been bothering me for a month.
Our scholarship fund shows forty students receiving full support. But I've been quietly matching the list against the class registers, and at least eleven of those names aren't enrolled anywhere. I've checked twice. I checked the old registers too, in case they'd left.
I keep asking myself whether I'm misunderstanding. Maybe there's a separate list I haven't seen. Maybe the principal has an explanation. She's been good to me; she hired me when nobody else would.
But there are real children on the waiting list for those scholarships. I've seen them in the office with their mothers.
I'm not doing anything yet. I just want to be completely sure before I say a word to anyone. Can you look at my notes this weekend and tell me if I'm seeing things?
Lalremsiami

qa.q: How many names aren't enrolled anywhere?
qa.a: At least eleven of those names.

qa.q: What is Lalremsiami feeling while writing?
qa.a: Lalremsiami feels doubtful and torn, wanting to be sure before acting and loyal to the principal who gave a job.

qa.q: Why is checking the facts first a wise step?
qa.a: Being sure it is real, by matching registers and getting a second view, protects everyone before any accusation is made.

qa.q: What might Nandini feel being asked to check the notes?
qa.a: Nandini likely feels trusted and concerned, ready to give an honest, sensible second opinion.

grounding: An accountant quietly gathers facts on possible scholarship misuse, asks whether the facts are misunderstood, and weighs loyalty against the children affected.

passage:
Ritu, I need to think out loud. I handle the emissions data at the plant. Last month the numbers we sent to the pollution board looked lower than what I remembered from the raw sensor logs. So I started checking. Quietly.
I've pulled six months of logs. In four of them the reported numbers are lower than the sensors, sometimes by half. Maybe there's a correction factor I don't know about. Maybe the sensors are faulty and someone adjusted for it. Meanwhile, on every shift I work, I make sure the backup filter is running.
The people involved are my friends. My boss covered for me when my mother was sick. But the village next to our plant has children coughing every winter.
I'm not ready to say anything yet. First I need to be sure. Can you help me go through the calibration sheets tomorrow? I'm Arnab, and right now I just need someone to tell me whether I'm reading this right.

qa.q: How many months of logs did Arnab pull?
qa.a: Six months of logs.

qa.q: What does Arnab feel about the boss?
qa.a: Arnab feels loyal and torn, grateful for past kindness yet uneasy about the children coughing near the plant.

qa.q: Why is Arnab right to check before acting?
qa.a: Confirming the pattern with the logs and a second reader makes sure it is real before raising it.

qa.q: What might Ritu feel being asked to help?
qa.a: Ritu probably feels trusted and a little anxious, aware of how serious the numbers could be.

grounding: An employee quietly checks emissions data, looks for innocent explanations and weighs loyalty against the neighbours who may be harmed.

passage:
Monday. Mahima, processing expenses at the Chennai office, noticed that her team lead's travel claims included a client visit to Coimbatore on a day he had been sitting two desks away from her. She told herself she had misremembered.
Wednesday. She checked the office entry logs. He had badged in at 9:02 that day. She checked the client's visitor records, which were shared for billing. No visit. Her hands went cold.
Friday. She found two more. She asked Hrithik from finance a careful question: could a claim be filed for a trip that was cancelled? "Only if it's refunded," he said. None had been.
Sunday. She sat with her notes and felt the weight of it. He had trained her. He had sent flowers when her father died. But the money came from a budget meant for the whole team's training. She wasn't ready to report anyone. She wanted to be certain, and she almost was.

qa.q: When did the team lead badge in that day?
What does Mahima feel on Sunday with her notes?
qa.a: She feels heavy and conflicted, grateful to her team lead but troubled by the evidence.

qa.q: What is wise about how Mahima is proceeding?
qa.a: She quietly checks entry logs, visitor records and finance rules, making sure it is real before deciding to act.

qa.q: What might Hrithik think about Mahima's careful question?
qa.a: Hrithik may sense something behind it and feel curious or concerned, while answering factually.

grounding: Over a week an employee quietly checks a trusted lead's claims, doubts herself, and weighs loyalty against the team the money was meant for.

passage: "Himani, come, sit with your old Rafiq Chacha. You asked what I did at the cement plant when I was your age. I was twenty-six, a junior engineer. I noticed the stack emission readings in the report were always the same, day after day. Too neat. My first thought was, I'm new, I'm misunderstanding something. So I didn't run to anyone. For two months I kept my own notebook. I checked the raw sensor logs at night. I asked the senior technician, casually, how the readings were entered. He said, 'We copy the good day.' Even then I thought of my colleagues, good men with families, and of the people in the village downwind, coughing every winter. I went round and round. I only decided to act when I was sure, with the logs in my own hand, and that same year the filters were fixed. Remember that part, beti. Be sure first."

qa.q: How long did Rafiq keep his own notebook?
qa.a: He kept his own notebook for two months.

qa.q: What was Rafiq feeling as he went round and round?
qa.a: Rafiq felt torn and doubtful, loyal to colleagues with families but worried about the village people coughing downwind.

qa.q: In the story, which choice made Rafiq's later action stronger?
qa.a: Quietly checking the raw sensor logs and keeping his own notebook until he was sure meant he acted on facts, not suspicion.

qa.q: How might the people in the village downwind have been affected by the copied readings?
qa.a: They were breathing whatever the plant released while the reports showed a good day, so their coughing every winter was going unexplained.

grounding: Shows a person quietly gathering facts, questioning whether they misunderstand and weighing loyalty to colleagues against people who may be harmed before acting.
